subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected, skipped, queued, or remain parallel by default, and should any 409 behavior be opt-in?
rationale: The requested 409 response changes an external webhook response contract and retry semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the default compatibility and security policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Opt-In Overlap Policy
options.body: Preserve the current 200/runId default and add configured reject, skip, or queue semantics for trusted hook sessions with documented retry behavior.

options.title: Default 409 Conflict
options.body: Reject same-session active hook deliveries by default, accepting that existing integrations may need migration to avoid retry loops.

options.title: Fold Into Queue Design
options.body: Defer this item into the broader queued webhook ingestion design so durable backlog and concurrency semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Opt-In Overlap Policy
recommendation.body: Preserve the current 200/runId default and add configured reject, skip, or queue semantics for trusted hook sessions with documented retry behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the clearest product/security policy owner from prior review discussion and recent adjacent hook/session history.
